review.summary: Mercedes lead the constructors' standings with 652 points from 20 rounds, 12 wins and 24 podiums. Andrea Kimi Antonelli tops the drivers' championship ahead of George Russell, and the pair have supplied most of the team's points through consistent finishes across the season.
review.lastRace: At the Brazilian Grand Prix, George Russell finished fourth from seventh on the grid to claim 12 points, while Andrea Kimi Antonelli took fifth from second and scored 10. Both drivers completed the race.

review.summary: Ferrari sit second in the constructors' standings with 510 points after 20 rounds and 13 podiums. Lewis Hamilton leads the pair narrowly ahead of Charles Leclerc in the drivers' championship, and their points have accumulated steadily through a season of two race wins.
review.lastRace: At the Brazilian Grand Prix, Charles Leclerc finished eighth from fourteenth on the grid for 4 points, while Lewis Hamilton dropped to ninth from the back of the grid and was lapped, taking 2 points.

review.summary: Red Bull are third in the constructors' standings with 415 points from 20 rounds and 15 podiums. Max Verstappen is their leading driver, well clear of Isack Hadjar and Liam Lawson in the drivers' championship, and his results have supplied most of the team's points.
review.lastRace: At the Brazilian Grand Prix, Max Verstappen recovered from twenty-first on the grid to finish second and take 18 points, while Isack Hadjar completed the podium with third from fifth for 15 points. Both finished.

review.summary: McLaren are fourth in the constructors' standings with 398 points after 20 rounds and eight podiums. Lando Norris leads the team ahead of Oscar Piastri in the drivers' championship, and their points have come from a mix of wins and consistent finishes across the season.
review.lastRace: At the Brazilian Grand Prix, Lando Norris won from pole position to take 25 points, while Oscar Piastri finished sixth from tenth for 8 points. Both completed the race.

review.summary: RB F1 Team are fifth in the constructors' standings with 114 points after 20 rounds but have taken no wins and no podiums. Arvid Lindblad is their leading driver, well ahead of Yuki Tsunoda, whose points tally has barely moved.
review.lastRace: At the Brazilian Grand Prix, Liam Lawson finished seventh from third to score 6 points, while Arvid Lindblad dropped to eleventh from eighteenth and was lapped without scoring.

review.summary: Alpine are sixth in the constructors' standings with 69 points after 20 rounds and no wins or podiums. Pierre Gasly leads the team ahead of Franco Colapinto, but their points have come only from mid-field finishes rather than results near the front.
review.lastRace: At the Brazilian Grand Prix, both Alpine cars were lapped: Franco Colapinto finished thirteenth from thirteenth on the grid and Pierre Gasly fourteenth from fifteenth, with neither scoring a point.

review.summary: Haas are seventh in the constructors' standings with 31 points after 20 rounds and no wins or podiums. Oliver Bearman is their leading driver by a wide margin ahead of Esteban Ocon, while Ryo Hirakawa and Rafael Camara have contributed little to the tally.
review.lastRace: At the Brazilian Grand Prix, Oliver Bearman fell to seventeenth from sixth on the grid and was lapped, while Rafael Camara finished twentieth from eleventh; both failed to score.

review.summary: Audi are eighth in the constructors' standings with 28 points after 20 rounds and no wins or podiums. Nico Hülkenberg and Gabriel Bortoleto are level on points in the drivers' championship, having gathered their scores from mid-field finishes rather than front-running results.
review.lastRace: At the Brazilian Grand Prix, Nico Hülkenberg finished tenth from fourth to take a single point while lapped, and Gabriel Bortoleto dropped to sixteenth from nineteenth without scoring.

review.summary: Williams are ninth in the constructors' standings with 12 points after 20 rounds and no wins or podiums. Carlos Sainz leads the team narrowly ahead of Alexander Albon in the drivers' championship, though their combined points have been modest throughout.
review.lastRace: At the Brazilian Grand Prix, both Williams cars were lapped: Alexander Albon finished fifteenth from ninth and Carlos Sainz nineteenth from twelfth, with neither scoring.

review.summary: Aston Martin are tenth in the constructors' standings with just 7 points after 20 rounds and no wins or podiums. Fernando Alonso is their only points scorer, well ahead of Lance Stroll, who has failed to add to the tally.
review.lastRace: At the Brazilian Grand Prix, Fernando Alonso finished twelfth from eighth but was lapped without scoring, while Lance Stroll retired from sixteen of the grid and took no points.

review.summary: Cadillac are eleventh in the constructors' standings with zero points after 20 rounds and no wins or podiums. Neither Valtteri Bottas nor Sergio Pérez has scored a point this season.
review.lastRace: At the Brazilian Grand Prix, Sergio Pérez finished eighteenth from twenty-second but was lapped without scoring, while Valtteri Bottas did not start from seventeen and took no points.

review.summary: Ducati lead the teams' standings after 19 rounds with eight wins and sixteen podiums. Marc Marquez tops the riders' championship on 431 points, clear of Fabio Di Giannantonio (282), with Alex Marquez (197) and Francesco Bagnaia (173) further back.
review.lastRace: In the Grand Prix of Qatar, Marc Marquez finished second for 20 points; Fabio Di Giannantonio eighth (8), Iker Lecuona tenth (6), Franco Morbidelli eleventh (5) and Fermin Aldeguer twelfth (4).

review.summary: Aprilia are the 2nd-ranked manufacturer in MotoGP after 19 rounds, with 9 wins and 33 podiums. Jorge Martin is their best-placed rider, 2nd overall.
review.lastRace: At the Grand Prix of Qatar, Marco Bezzecchi finished 1st; Raul Fernandez finished 3rd; Ai Ogura finished 4th; Jorge Martin finished 7th.

review.summary: KTM are third after 19 rounds with two wins and eight podiums. Pedro Acosta leads their riders on 309 points in fourth overall, well ahead of Enea Bastianini (147) and Brad Binder (118). Maverick Viñales (17), Pol Espargaro (5) and Jonas Folger (0) trail.
review.lastRace: In the Grand Prix of Qatar, Enea Bastianini finished fifth for 11 points and Pedro Acosta sixth (10), with Maverick Viñales thirteenth (3). Brad Binder retired without scoring.

review.summary: Honda remain fourth after 19 rounds with no wins and no podiums. Luca Marini are their best-placed rider on 117 points in thirteenth, ahead of Diogo Moreira (78) and Johann Zarco (63). Joan Mir (33) and the rest score little down the field.
review.lastRace: Johann Zarco finished ninth for seven points in the Grand Prix of Qatar, with Jake Dixon fourteenth (2). Diogo Moreira retired without scoring.

review.summary: Yamaha are fifth after 19 rounds with no wins and no podiums. Fabio Quartararo leads their riders on 79 points in fourteenth, ahead of Jack Miller (31), Alex Rins (29) and Toprak Razgatlioglu (18). Augusto Fernandez (6) is the lowest-scoring rider listed.

Jaguar lead the championship with 288 points from 17 rounds, four wins and ten podiums. Evans tops their tally on 160 as third in the standings, while Da Costa sits sixth on 128. Their London E-Prix saw Evans finish fourth for twelve points after starting fifth, but Da Costa slipped to fifteenth from ninth without scoring.
review.lastRace: At the London E-Prix, Mitch Evans finished fourth, starting fifth, taking twelve points, while António Félix Da Costa dropped to fifteenth from a ninth-place grid slot and scored nothing.

review.summary: Porsche sit second with 271 points across 17 rounds, four wins and eight podiums. Wehrlein leads their drivers on 169 as championship runner-up, well clear of Müller on 102 in ninth. London was a quiet one for both, each finishing without points.
review.lastRace: At the London E-Prix, Nico Müller ended twelfth from a fourth-place grid slot and Pascal Wehrlein fourteenth after starting third; neither scored a point.

review.summary: Mahindra are third on 252 points from 17 rounds with two wins and seven podiums. Mortara leads the pair on 137 as fifth in the standings, ahead of De Vries on 115 in seventh. London delivered a strong double podium for both drivers.
review.lastRace: Nyck De Vries took second off the front grid slot for twenty-one points at the London E-Prix, with teammate Edoardo Mortara third from second for fifteen.

review.summary: Andretti sit fourth with 229 points across 17 rounds, two wins and seven podiums. Dennis is their strongest driver on 164 as second overall, far ahead of Drugovich on 65 in fourteen. London was a poor outing for both, neither reaching the points.
review.lastRace: At the London E-Prix, Jake Dennis finished eighteenth after starting sixteenth and Felipe Drugovich thirteenth from eleventh; neither scored.

review.summary: Citroën are fifth on 182 points from 17 rounds with one win and six podiums. Cassidy leads the pair on 114 as eighth in the standings, ahead of Vergne on 68 in twelfth. Both collected points at the London E-Prix.
review.lastRace: Nick Cassidy finished sixth, starting seventh for eight points, and Jean-Éric Vergne seventh after a twelve-place grid start took six at the London E-Prix.

review.summary: Nissan sit sixth with 157 points across 17 rounds, one win and six podiums. Rowland are their leading driver on 137 as fourth overall, well clear of Nato on 20 in nineteenth. Each scored a point at the London E-Prix.
review.lastRace: Oliver Rowland finished ninth after starting seventeenth for three points, with Norman Nato tenth from nineteenth taking one at the London E-Prix.

review.summary: Envision are seventh on 152 points from 17 rounds with no wins and two podiums. Buemi lead the pair on 97 as tenth in the standings, ahead of Eriksson on 55 in sixteenth. London saw Buemi finish fifth for ten points, while Eriksson started fifteenth but left the classification unplaced.
review.lastRace: Sébastien Buemi finished fifth after starting tenth for ten points at the London E-Prix, while teammate Joel Eriksson started fifteenth but left the classification without a position.

review.summary: Cupra Kiro sit eighth with 128 points across 17 rounds, one win and three podiums. Martí lead the pair on 66 as thirteenth in the standings, just ahead of Ticktum on 62 in fifteenth. Martí reached the points at London while Ticktum fell back from an eighth-place grid slot.
review.lastRace: Josep Maria Martí finished eighth after starting thirteenth for four points at the London E-Prix, but Dan Tumtum started eighth and fell to sixteenth without scoring.

review.summary: DS Penske are ninth on 91 points from 17 rounds with one win and a single podium. Barnard lead the pair on 68 as eleventh in the standings, ahead of Günther on 23 in eighteenth. London saw Barnard take the race win for twenty-five points while Günther finished eleventh without scoring.
review.lastRace: Taylor Barnard won the London E-Prix, starting sixth for twenty-five points, while Maximilian Günther finished eleventh after a fourteenth-place grid slot and scored nothing.

review.summary: Lola Yamaha ABT are tenth on 35 points from 17 rounds with one win and a single podium. Di Grassi lead the pair on 32 as seventeenth in the standings, far ahead of Maloney on 3 in twentieth. Neither added to their tally at London.
review.lastRace: At the London E-Prix, Zane Maloney finished seventeenth from eighteenth without scoring, while Lucas Di Grassi started twentieth but left the classification unplaced.

Third on 262 points after 20 rounds, with three wins and eight podiums, so he sits behind teammate Andrea Kimi Antonelli. He started seventh and finished fourth in the Brazilian Grand Prix, scoring twelve points.

Fourth on 261 points after 20 rounds, with one win and seven podiums, so he sits just ahead of teammate Charles Leclerc. In the Brazilian Grand Prix he started from last on the grid (twentieth) and was lapped as he finished ninth, taking two points.

Fifth on 249 points after 20 rounds, with one win and six podiums, so he sits just behind teammate Lewis Hamilton. He started fourteenth and finished eighth in the Brazilian Grand Prix, scoring four points.
Max Verstappen is 2nd in the Formula 1 standings on 279 points for Red Bull, with 3 wins and 12 podiums this season. At the Brazilian Grand Prix they finished 2nd from 21st on the grid.

Eighth on 122 points after 20 rounds, with no wins but three podiums. He sits well behind teammate Max Verstappen in the standings. In the Brazilian Grand Prix he started fifth and finished third to take fifteen points.

On 246 points after 20 rounds, Lando Norris sits sixth with three wins and six podiums at McLaren. In the Brazilian Grand Prix he started first and won, scoring twenty-five points.

Sixteenth in the standings with 7 points from 20 rounds, no wins and no podiums. He trails team-mate Oliver Bearman, who has 23 points.

Bottas sits 23rd on zero points behind team-mate Pérez, without a win or podium. He started 17th in Brazil but did not start the race.

Sergio Pérez sits 24th in the standings with zero points from 20 rounds, having won nothing and never reached a podium. At the Brazilian Grand Prix he started from slot 22 and finished 18th, lapped off the lead lap. He shares the Cadillac F1 Team seat with team-mate Valtteri Bottas.

Marc Marquez leads with 431 points from 19 rounds, seven wins and eight podiums, clear at the top of the Ducati standings ahead of teammates Fabio Di Giannantonio (sixth) and Alex Marquez (eighth). His latest race was a second place at the Grand Prix of Qatar, earning 20 points.

Fabio Di Giannantonio is sixth with 282 points from 19 rounds and two podiums, still without a win. He trails Marquez comfortably but holds a clear margin over the rest of the Ducati line-up. His latest race was eighth at the Grand Prix of Qatar, taking 8 points.

Jorge Martin sits second in the standings with 371 points from 19 rounds, one win and ten podiums. His most recent race ended seventh at the Grand Prix of Qatar for nine points.
Marco Bezzecchi is third with 357 points across 19 rounds, six wins and twelve podiums — ahead of team-mate Jorge Martin. He won the Grand Prix of Qatar for 25 points last time out.
Ai Ogura sits fifth with 294 points from 19 rounds, one win and four podiums. He finished fourth at the Grand Prix of Qatar last time out for 13 points.
Raul Fernandez is seventh with 258 points across 19 rounds, one win and seven podiums. He took third at the Grand Prix of Qatar for 16 points in his most recent race.
Lorenzo Savadori sits 31st with zero points from 19 rounds and no wins or podiums this season.
Pedro Acosta is fourth with 309 points from 19 rounds, two wins and eight podiums. He finished sixth at the Grand Prix of Qatar for 10 points last time out.
Enea Bastianini sits tenth with 147 points across 19 rounds and no wins or podiums. He finished fifth at the Grand Prix of Qatar for 11 points in his most recent race.
Brad Binder sits twelfth with 118 points across 19 rounds and no wins or podiums. He scored nothing at the Grand Prix of Qatar in his most recent race.

Viñales sits 23rd with 17 points from 19 rounds and no wins or podiums. In the Grand Prix of Qatar he finished 13th for three points (INSTND). He is ahead of teammate Jonas Folger, who has yet to score.

Joan Mir is 18th in the MotoGP standings on 33 points for Honda.
Somkiat Chantra is 26th in the MotoGP standings on 3 points for Honda.

Twenty-seventh after nineteen rounds with three points and neither a win nor a podium. He trails team-mate Jake Dixon, who has two points and a fourteenth-place finish at the Grand Prix of Qatar, but stays ahead of Cal Crutchlow and Aleix Espargaro, both on zero.

Twenty-eighth after nineteen rounds with two points and neither a win nor a podium. At the Grand Prix of Qatar he recorded a fourteenth-place finish for those two points from an unlisted grid slot, sitting just behind team-mate Takaaki Nakagami in the standings.

Twenty-ninth after nineteen rounds with zero points and neither a win nor a podium. He sits level on zero with team-mate Aleix Espargaro, both below Takaaki Nakagami and Jake Dixon, who have each scored this season.

Fourteenth after nineteen rounds with 79 points and neither a win nor a podium. He is clear of team-mate Jack Miller (31) and Alex Rins (29), and also ahead of Toprak Razgatlioglu, his leading teammate on points.

Twentieth after nineteen rounds with 29 points, neither a win nor a podium. He sits behind team-mates Fabio Quartararo (79) and Jack Miller (31), just clear of Toprak Razgatlioglu (18).
Twenty-second after nineteen rounds with 18 points, no wins and no podiums. He sits behind team-mates Fabio Quartararo (79), Jack Miller (31) and Alex Rins (29).

Third in the standings with 160 points from 17 rounds and two wins. Five podiums back his season, and he holds a margin over team-mate António Félix Da Costa. At the London E-Prix he started fifth and finished fourth to take 12 points.

Sixth in the standings with 128 points from 17 rounds and two wins. Five podiums match team-mate Mitch Evans, though he sits behind him on points. His London E-Prix ended poorly, starting ninth and fading to fifteenth for no points.

Leading the championship with 169 points from 17 rounds and three wins. Six podiums back his top spot, and he holds a clear edge over team-mate Nico Müller. The London E-Prix was a disappointment, starting third but fading to fourteenth for no points.

Ninth in the standings with 102 points from 17 rounds and one win. Two podiums leave him well behind team-mate Pascal Wehrlein at the top of the table. He started fourth at the London E-Prix but fell to twelfth for no points.

Fifth in the standings with 137 points from 17 rounds but no wins. Three podiums back his season, and he sits ahead of team-mate Nyck De Vries. The London E-Prix rewarded him well, starting second and finishing third for 15 points.

Seventh in the standings with 115 points from 17 rounds and two wins. Four podiums leave him behind team-mate Edoardo Mortara on points. The London E-Prix was his best round, starting on pole and finishing second for 21 points.

Second in the standings with 164 points from 17 rounds and two wins. Six podiums keep him close to the leader but well ahead of team-mate Felipe Drugovich. The London E-Prix was a low point, starting sixteenth and finishing eighteenth for no points.

Fourteenth in the standings with 65 points from 17 rounds and one podium. He trails team-mate Jake Dennis through the standings. The London E-Prix offered little, starting eleventh and finishing thirteenth for no points.

Cassidy leads Citroën's charge with 114 points from 17 rounds after one win and five podiums, sitting four places above teammate Jean-Éric Vergne. His London E-Prix brought a sixth-place finish from seventh on the grid, adding eight more points.

Vergne sits twelfth with 68 points across 17 rounds and one podium, without a win. He tears teammate Nick Cassidy by 46 points after a London E-Prix that started at fifteenth on the grid and finished seventh for six points.

Rowland tops Nissan with 137 points from 17 rounds, one win and six podiums, fourth overall. He outpoints teammate Norman Nato by a wide margin. His London E-Prix recovered from seventeenth on the grid to ninth for three points.

Nato sits nineteenth with just 20 points from 17 rounds and no wins or podiums, far behind teammate Oliver Rowland. His London E-Prix began at the back of the grid in nineteenth and recovered to tenth for a single point.

Buemi sits tenth with 97 points from 17 rounds and one podium, without a win. He leads teammate Joel Eriksson in Envision's standings. His London E-Prix finished fifth from tenth on the grid for ten points.

Eriksson sits sixteenth with 55 points from 17 rounds and one podium, without a win, behind teammate Sébastien Buemi. His London E-Prix started at fifteenth on the grid but did not reach the flag for any points.

Martí sits thirteenth with 66 points from 17 rounds and two podiums, without a win. He edges out teammate Dan Ticktum in Cupra Kiro's standings. His London E-Prix finished eighth from thirteenth on the grid for four points.
Ticktum sits fifteenth with 62 points from 17 rounds after one win and one podium, behind teammate Josep Maria Martí. His London E-Prix fell back from eighth on the grid to sixteenth for no points.

Barnard sits 11th with 68 points from 17 rounds after one win and a podium. He leads his DS Penske teammate Maximilian Günther comfortably, closing the season by winning the London E-Prix from sixth on the grid.
Günther is 18th with 23 points from 17 rounds and no wins or podiums. He trails teammate Taylor Barnard by a wide margin, finishing 11th off the grid in the London E-Prix without scoring.

review.summary: Maloney is 20th with just 3 points from 17 rounds and no wins or podiums. He clearly trails teammate Lucas Di Grassi, finishing 17th off the grid in the London E-Prix without scoring.

Lando Norris of McLaren won from pole ahead of a Red Bull one-two, with Max Verstappen recovering from twenty-first to finish second and Isack Hadjar third from fifth. The classification shows Mercedes' Andrea Kimi Antonelli taking the fastest lap in fifth, while Lance Stroll retired and Valtteri Bottas did not start.
highlights: Max Verstappen started twenty-first on the grid and finished second behind Lando Norris.
Andrea Kimi Antonelli took the fastest lap of the race while finishing fifth for Mercedes.
Lance Stroll retired from sixteen of the grid and did not complete the race.
Valtteri Bottas did not start from seventeen of the grid for Cadillac.

review.summary: Marco Bezzecchi won for Aprilia Racing, with Ducatis' Marc Marquez second and Raul Fernandez of SuperFile Trackhouse MotoGP Team completing the podium. The classification shows SuperFile Trackhouse in two of the top four positions, while Brad Binder and Diogo Moreira both retired without scoring.
highlights: Marco Bezzecchi won the Grand Prix of Qatar for Aprilia Racing on 25 points.
SuperFile Trackhouse MotoGP Team finished third and fourth through Raul Fernandez and Ai Ogura.
Brad Binder and Diogo Moreira both retired without scoring a point.

review.summary: Barnard climbed from sixth to claim victory for DS Penske at the London E-Prix, taking twenty-five points. Mahindra secured a two-car podium with Nyck De Vries second after starting on pole and Edoardo Mortara third from second. Sébastien Buemi fifth and Nick Cassidy sixth completed the points.
highlights: Norman Nato made the biggest climb of the race, moving from nineteenth to finish tenth.
Taylor Barnard won the London E-Prix, climbing from sixth to take twenty-five points for DS Penske.
Nyck De Vries started from pole and finished second for Mahindra Racing, one place behind the winner.
